    Tentative itinerary, day by day

    Mon–Thu are visit days, one cluster per half-day, with student societies hosting evenings at Oxford Edge. Fri–Sun is ETO West itself. Timings within each day are indicative only.

    Mon 8 Nov

    Arrival & orientation

    Base day · Oxford Edge
    Afternoon
    Welcome & orientation at Oxford EdgeBase

    37 St Giles — the university's entrepreneurship centre, with a hardware lab and a track record of hosting student groups and societies. Week briefing, team introductions, walking-tour ground rules.

    Evening
    Society welcome sessionProspective co-organizers

    An opening session hosted with Oxford student societies — OxCyS (Oxford Cybersecurity Society), OxAI and the Oxford Blockchain Society are the natural partners for the three Olympiad themes. OxCyS is our leading co-organizer candidate; none of the societies is confirmed yet.

    Tue 9 Nov

    Quantum & cyber — the Parks Road cluster

    All on foot · ≤10 min between stops
    The Clarendon Laboratory, Parks Road. Photo: Wikimedia Commons.
    Morning
    Clarendon Laboratory — University PhysicsIQCOLTo request

    Home to Oxford's Ion Trap, Superconducting Quantum Devices and Optical Quantum Technologies groups — the lab Oxford Quantum Circuits and Oxford Ionics spun out of. Its hands-on “How to Build a Quantum Computer” workshop is sized for ~30, an exact fit for our group; an on-site version would be a bespoke outreach request.

    Cyber Security Oxford / ACE-CSR — Dept of Computer ScienceIBCOLTo request

    An NCSC/EPSRC Academic Centre of Excellence in Cyber Security Research, a few steps from the Clarendon. The strongest academic cyber talk host on the route, and the natural pairing for an OxCyS co-organized session.

    Lunch
    Covered Market~10 min walk

    50+ traders under one roof with central picnic tables — the group splits across tables. No booking needed.

    Afternoon
    Oxford e-Research Centre (OeRC)IDSOLTo request

    7 Keble Road — data science and research software engineering, with a regular programme of courses, training and events.

    Reuben CollegeIDSOLTo request

    Parks Road — Oxford's newest college, founded around AI & machine learning and ethics, with a public-engagement focus. The least-evidenced visit on this list; needs a direct approach.

    Wed 10 Nov

    Data, AI & society — Broad Street to the Observatory Quarter

    All on foot
    The Schwarzman Centre, now home to the Oxford Internet Institute and the Institute for Ethics in AI. Photo © David Levene, via Building Magazine.
    Morning
    Oxford Martin School + AI Governance InitiativeIDSOLPublic lectures

    34 Broad Street — a public, registration-based lecture programme in a central theatre. The easiest stop on the whole itinerary to seat 20–30 people into: book seats rather than request a tour.

    Schwarzman Centre — Oxford Internet Institute & Institute for Ethics in AIIDSOLIBCOL policyTo request

    Both institutes moved into the new Stephen A. Schwarzman Centre in the Radcliffe Observatory Quarter (Oct 2025) — social data science and AI/LLMs on one side, ethics-in-AI seminars and panels on the other, in a single building.

    Lunch
    Gloucester Green Market~7 min walk

    Street food and benches. Runs Wed–Sat only, lunch only, and it's weather-exposed — Wednesday is the day in our week when it's on. Covered Market is the wet-weather fallback.

    Afternoon
    Oxford Science Enterprises (OSE)To request

    46 Woodstock Road — the investor behind Oxford's spinout pipeline (~£850m raised, 125+ companies). A “how spinouts get funded” talk rather than a lab tour; useful context for teams thinking about what happens after the Olympiad.

    Thu 11 Nov

    Fintech & post-quantum — Jericho and Summertown

    Decided · stays in Oxford
    Morning
    Oxford-Man Institute of Quantitative FinanceIDSOLIBCOLTo request

    Eagle House, Walton Well Road, Jericho (~10 min walk). Machine learning for quantitative finance, with Man Group's research lab in-house — and a research line in blockchain economics and DeFi. The single best bridge between the data and blockchain themes.

    Afternoon — Summertown
    Mind Foundry — SummertownIDSOLTo request

    Ewert House, Summertown (~25 min walk up Banbury Road). Oxford ML spinout building AI for high-stakes settings — defence and security, insurance, infrastructure.

    PQShield — SummertownIQCOLIBCOLTo request

    Prama House, Banbury Road (~35–40 min walk, or a short bus from the centre). Post-quantum cryptography and a major contributor to the NIST PQC standards — the defensive answer to “quantum breaks encryption”, pairing naturally with Tuesday's quantum morning. Office visit: a talk, not a lab tour.

    Decided: Thursday stays in Summertown — Oxford-Man Institute in the morning, then Mind Foundry and PQShield. No Harwell trip. The day needs no transport beyond the long walk up Banbury Road (or a short bus back).
    Fri 12 – Sun 14 Nov

    ETO West 2027

    Oxford Edge · all three days
    Emerging Tech Olympiads — WestVenue to confirm

    The reason for the week: the IBCOL, IDSOL and IQCOL finals programme at Oxford Edge, 37 St Giles. The Mon–Thu visits are deliberately themed to feed into these three days — quantum and cyber on Tuesday, data and AI governance on Wednesday, fintech and post-quantum on Thursday. The detailed ETO schedule is a separate document; this page covers the surrounding week only.

    Two possible shapes — to be confirmed: Friday depends on whether the Oxford Saïd Entrepreneurship Forum (OSEF) is confirmed as the official partner event.

    Branch A — if OSEF confirms: Fri 12 Nov is the Oxford Saïd Entrepreneurship Forum as ERTW's official partner event. ETO West then runs only Sat 13 Nov (Opening Ceremony and Exhibition Day) and Sun 14 Nov (Pitch Day and Closing Ceremony).

    Branch B — if OSEF does not confirm: Fri 12 Nov is the ETO Opening Ceremony and Welcome Party, at Oxford Edge; Sat 13 Nov is Exhibition Day; Sun 14 Nov is Pitch Day and Closing Ceremony.

    Shortlist & alternates

    Held in reserve if a first-choice host declines, a slot opens up, or a theme needs more depth. Same status as everything else here: not approached yet, unless noted.

    • Quantum DiceIQCOLIBCOL

      Central Oxford. Student-founded spinout making quantum random number generators for cybersecurity — the most relatable “students → startup” story on the list. Small team, so a talk / Q&A is realistic; a lab tour is uncertain. Address listings vary — confirm before approaching.

    • DiffblueIDSOL

      St Ebbes / Worcester Place (verify address). AI that writes Java unit tests, used by major banks. Small office — talk or demo request only.

    • CDL-Oxford — Saïd Business SchoolIDSOLIBCOL

      Park End Street. Creative Destruction Lab's Oxford site runs AI and FinTech streams. Cohort sessions are closed, so the ask would be a guest talk or venture showcase. (The Oxford Foundry has closed into Saïd's Entrepreneurship Centre — CDL / Saïd is the current route.)

    • Oxford Ionics (now IonQ) — KidlingtonIQCOL

      Oxford Technology Park, ~6 miles north (~30 min bus). Trapped-ion quantum computing on semiconductor chips; its 30,000 sq ft HQ opened in March 2025 and hosted tours of 100+ guests at the opening — but access is invitation-only, and it would need a bus trip, so it sits outside the current walk-first plan.

    • Oxa (formerly Oxbotica) — CowleyIDSOL

      Oxford Business Park. Autonomous-vehicle software at scale-up stage — live AVs make this the highest-“wow” company visit on the list. Bus or taxi.

    • Big Data Institute — HeadingtonIDSOL

      Old Road Campus (~15–20 min bus). Very large health datasets and genomics — the strongest health-data stop, if the IDSOL teams want that angle.

    • Oxford University Innovation — invite in, don't visit

      The university's tech-transfer office (350+ spinouts). Better invited to speak at Oxford Edge than visited at its Botley office.

    Food & walking notes

    Food is included in the week; local transport is included too, and the plan spends as little of it as possible. Two realities shape both.

    Inside the Covered Market — Tuesday's lunch plan. Photo: The Oxford Magazine.

    Eating — the term-time reality

    Don't plan on college Formal Hall. ERTW week (8–14 Nov 2027) falls inside Oxford's Michaelmas Full Term (10 Oct – 4 Dec 2027). In term, college halls serve members and members' guests; the cheap hall prices you'll see published are member prices, and most hall dining for outside groups is vacation-only.
    • First ask — Christ Church, McKenna Room.

      Christ Church is Oxford Edge's own college. Its McKenna Room (not the Great Hall) takes private lunches and dinners Mon–Fri in term, minimum 20, seats 55; dinners from 8pm. Quote needed — not low-cost by default, but the right flagship option.

    • Also bookable in term — St Catherine's College.

      Term-time day conferences with hot hall lunches; no term-time dinners.

    • Daily low-cost, no booking.

      Covered Market (~10 min, split tables) and Gloucester Green Market (Wed–Sat lunches only, weather-exposed) cover most days between them.

    • Cheapest pre-bookable — Taylors of Oxford catering.

      Delivered set menus from £9.95 per head for groups of 25+. Confirm Oxford Edge permits external catering and on what terms for an external organizer.

    Walking — distances from Oxford Edge

    • The core is genuinely walkable.

      Jericho ~8–10 min · Carfax / city centre ~10–12 min · Oxford station ~12–15 min · every Tue–Wed stop ≤20 min. No transport budget needed Mon–Wed.

    • Summertown is the stretch.

      ~25 min to Mind Foundry, ~35–40 min to PQShield on foot — fine one way for a fit group of students, with a short bus back as the fallback.

    • Staying in Oxford — no excursions.

      The week makes no out-of-town trip: a Harwell excursion was considered and decided against, and Thursday stays in Summertown instead. Alternates in Kidlington, Cowley and Headington would need a bus and are not in the plan.

    • Group size helps.

      20–30 is within the hosted-group size several of these venues already handle — the Clarendon workshop format is built for ~30, and the McKenna Room minimum is 20.

    Notes & corrections for co-organizers

    Three things that changed while this shortlist was being checked — please don't plan around the older versions.

    Corrections

    • FLOxford is a community, not a venue or company.

      FLOxford is Oxford's Free/Libre & Open-Source Software (FLOSS) community — talks, workshops and socials at varying venues. A useful contact and an easy drop-in; it is not settled as host or partner, and can't be booked as a site visit.

    • Oxford Quantum Circuits is in Reading now, not Oxford.

      OQC has moved to Thames Valley Science Park, Reading. It is deliberately not in this itinerary; its story is covered where it started — the Clarendon Laboratory groups it spun out of (Tuesday).

    • Almost nothing here offers a standard group tour.

      With the exception of public lectures and seminars (Oxford Martin School, Schwarzman Centre), every visit is a bespoke talk/demo request to a host who hasn't been approached yet. Lead time matters — approaches should go out well ahead of November 2027.

      Thursday stays in Summertown: Oxford-Man Institute (Jericho) in the morning, then Mind Foundry and PQShield. No Harwell trip.
